item.title: SSH: Connecting to a Remote Server in Linux
item.description:
Introduction

Accessing machines remotely became a necessity a long time ago, and it is difficult to imagine managing computers without remote access. There are various ways to establish a connection with a remote machine, depending on the operating system in use. The two most commonly used protocols are:

  • Secure Shell (SSH) for Linux-based machines
  • Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for Windows-based machines

Both protocols use client and server applications to establish remote connections. These tools allow you to remotely manage other computers, transfer files, and perform any task that would be possible if you were physically in front of the machine.

item.title: Dual boot Ubuntu and Windows
item.description:
Introduction

In this guide, we will discuss how to dual boot Ubuntu side by side with Windows. Before we proceed, let’s briefly understand what Ubuntu is.

What is Ubuntu?

Ubuntu is a Linux distribution based on Debian, composed mostly of free and open-source software. It is a popular operating system for cloud computing, with support for OpenStack.

Ubuntu is developed by Canonical and a community of developers under a meritocratic governance model. Canonical provides security updates and support for each Ubuntu release until it reaches its designated end-of-life (EOL) date.
